why: A small design task: a dict token -> expiry time. generate sets expiry, renew updates it only while expiry > now, and count tallies tokens with expiry > now.
hints: You only need each token's current expiration time.
A token is alive at time t iff expiry > t (equal means expired). Renew checks that before resetting expiry to t + ttl.
Dict of token -> expiry; count scans the dict (or keep a sorted structure / heap with lazy deletion if counts are frequent). O(1) per generate/renew.
pitfalls: Expiry exactly equal to current_time is expired: it cannot be renewed or counted.
Renewing a missing or expired token does nothing (it does not create one).
Parse each query string by splitting on spaces; count has only one argument.
